title: Lower a tool chest lid by its side handle while its stay release is held
instruction: Close the orange lid of the grey tool chest by its side handle until it rests flat on its rim, then let go.
context: Shutting the lid of a hand-carry toolbox is something nearly every household does: in a garage, a shed or a van, the lid is propped open on a ratchet stay and has to be put down without letting it drop. One hand holds the stay's release knob pulled out while the other lowers the 1.3 kg lid by its side handle, slowly, since a lid that falls shut dents its rim, bounces and catches fingers at the gap and hinge. A home robot that tidies a workshop has to do this familiar chore.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475; arm bases at x 0, y +-0.305 (0.61 m apart, reach 0.35 m). One fixed assembly, a hand-carry tool chest. (1) Chest body: grey powder-coated steel, sRGB (0.55, 0.57, 0.60), 4.0 kg, fixed to the table; an open case 220 x 460 mm in plan (x 0.14 to 0.36, y -0.23 to 0.23), 160 mm high (rim at z 0.9075), 6 mm walls and floor; friction 0.8. (2) Lid: orange aluminium, sRGB (0.95, 0.50, 0.10), 1.3 kg, a 226 x 472 x 4 mm plate (y -0.236 to 0.236) with 3 x 20 mm lips down its front and both side edges, hinged on a horizontal line along y at x 0.36, z 0.9075 (damping 0.02 N m s/rad); friction 0.8. A flat 40 x 50 x 8 mm pull tab (the side handle) sticks out of the lid's right side, centred at y -0.261, 0.19 m from the hinge. (3) Ratchet lid stay (real build): a 3 x 12 x 160 mm steel flat bar with sawtooth teeth, 4 mm pitch, 1.5 mm deep, along its last 60 mm, pinned to the inside of the lid's left lip by a 3 mm pin 150 mm from the hinge line and 15 mm below the plate, and sliding through a guide block on the chest's left inner wall that pivots on a 3 mm pin 80 mm in front of the hinge line and 45 mm below the rim; the rod slides 31 mm between shut and 25 deg open. A 2 mm steel pawl, 10 mm wide, on a 3 mm pin in the guide bears on the teeth under a 0.3 N leaf spring: the teeth ramp over it as the lid is raised and block lowering. A 3:1 bellcrank (24 mm arm to the knob, 8 mm arm to the pawl tail) joins the pawl to a 3 mm pull rod through a 5 mm hole in the left end wall to the knob; 6 mm of knob travel lifts the pawl 2 mm, clear of the 1.5 mm teeth, and it drops back below 4 mm. The lid starts open 25 deg; it can be raised, but cannot go down unless the knob is out 6 mm or more. (4) Release knob: a red 10 x 60 x 30 mm spring-return pull tongue on the chest's left end wall, centred at x 0.20, y 0.26, z 0.8275, sliding out along y 0 to 20 mm (a collar on the pull rod stops it at 20 mm) against a 150 N/m extension spring on the pull rod, no preload (0.9 N at 6 mm, 2.1 N at 14 mm). With the knob out, the lid swings shut by itself. The left arm reaches only the knob and the right arm only the tab (each is 0.5 m or more from the other arm).
scoring: Every control step from reset a linkkit History (cleared only by the simulator reset) records the lid angle q (0 = plate on the rim), the free-edge speed (travel of the free edge over the last 0.25 s, 0.226 m from the hinge), the knob travel, and each gripper's pad-point clearance to the chest and speed. Gates, any time in the run, give 0: a free edge faster than 0.15 m/s (2.5 mm per frame at 60 fps), which is any slam or fast lowering (a dropped lid dents the rim and can hurt a hand); any pad point inside the lid's pinch zone: the gap under its plate (within 40 mm below the plate, over its footprint) or within 25 mm of its hinge line. Ladder: 0.25 = lid lowered below 20 deg (it can only leave its stay with the knob out); 0.5 = below 15 deg; 0.75 = lid shut at the end (q at most 0.6 deg, free edge within 2.4 mm of the rim); 1.0 = also lid still (under 5 mm/s) for 1 s and every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the chest, both grippers under 10 mm/s and the knob back home (under 2 mm) for 1 s (release gate). One arm alone scores 0: the tab arm alone cannot lower the lid off its stay, and the knob arm alone lets the lid fall shut (slam gate). Real trial: a protractor on the hinge (stay at 25 deg, rungs at 20 and 15 deg); a ruler on the knob (6 mm out frees the lid, under 2 mm is home); 60 fps video beside a mm scale for the free-edge travel (at most 37 mm in any 15 frames); a 2 mm feeler gauge that must not pass under the shut lid's free edge anywhere along its width; blue tape on the fingertips and tape lines on the chest (40 mm below the plate edge and a 25 mm band along the hinge) for the pinch gate, read from the video; a ruler for the 30 mm release clearance.
reset_notes: Raise the lid to 25 deg (protractor on the hinge); the pawl catches it. Let the knob spring home (under 2 mm on the ruler). Nothing is consumed; the chest is fixed on taped outlines.
fidelity: Real stay: a 3 x 12 x 160 mm toothed steel rod (4 mm pitch) pinned to the lid, sliding in a guide on the left wall; a spring pawl bears on its teeth; a 3:1 bellcrank on a 3 mm pull rod to the knob lifts it 2 mm. Simulated as a hinge limit that lifts with the knob (6 mm out) and catches below 4 mm. Chest 160 mm, 4 kg, empty; lid a rigid plate on a pin hinge; no latch or contents.
